title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self: Misuse of Human Faculties and Their 2 Main Purposes

questions.question: How did the sinful group respond to the signs that point to Allah’s oneness when they entered worldly life with moral responsibility?
questions.answer: They met those signs with disbelief and refusal.

questions.question: How did they treat the blessings around them?
questions.answer: They were ungrateful for them.

questions.question: What wrong did they do toward other creatures besides being ungrateful?
questions.answer: They looked down on creation and treated it as if it had no worth.

questions.question: Why does the passage describe their wrongdoing as extremely great even though their life is short?
questions.answer: Because they denied the divine names and misused the life and abilities given to them for higher purposes.

questions.question: What mistaken idea about life is challenged in the passage?
questions.answer: The idea that life is only for comfort, civilization, and pleasing physical desires.

questions.question: According to the passage, are human senses and abilities mainly for satisfying the lower self? Explain.
questions.answer: No. They were given for much greater purposes than feeding low desires in a temporary life.

questions.question: What is the first main aim of the human faculties?
questions.answer: To recognize Allah’s blessings and respond with thanks and worship.

questions.question: What is the second main aim of the human faculties?
questions.answer: To notice the signs of Allah’s names in the world, experience them, and come to faith through that recognition.

questions.question: What happens to a person who fulfills these two main aims?
questions.answer: The person grows, becomes complete, and reaches true human character.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the connection between recognizing blessings and worship?
questions.answer: Seeing blessings properly should lead a person to thank Allah and worship Him.

questions.question: How does experiencing the signs of Allah’s names help a person?
questions.answer: It helps the person know them more deeply and strengthens belief.

questions.question: What is the main message of this passage?
questions.answer: Human life and abilities are a trust meant for faith, gratitude, and worship, not just worldly pleasure.

questions.question: Who is being described at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The group made up of sinners and wicked people.

questions.question: At what stage of life do they become responsible for their response?
questions.answer: When they reach the age at which they can understand and are accountable.

questions.question: Name two ways they responded wrongly to what Allah placed around them.
questions.answer: They denied the signs of His unity and they showed ingratitude for His blessings.

questions.question: What attitude did they show toward creation itself?
questions.answer: They insulted creation by acting as if it were meaningless and worthless.

questions.question: Why does the passage say they deserve endless punishment?
questions.answer: Because they rejected the manifestations of the divine names and committed a huge offense with the gifts they had been given.

questions.question: What were life and human abilities originally given for?
questions.answer: They were given for the duties and responsibilities of human beings before Allah.

questions.question: What kind of question is asked to wake up the reader from heedlessness?
questions.answer: Whether a person thinks life is only for enjoyment and feeding bodily wants.

questions.question: How does the passage describe worldly life when compared with the purpose of the human being?
questions.answer: It describes worldly life as temporary and not the final goal.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the finer human senses and feelings?
questions.answer: They are delicate and meaningful gifts, not tools made only for low desires.

questions.question: What is the first major purpose of these faculties?
questions.answer: To let a person recognize many kinds of blessings from the True Giver and respond with thanks.

questions.question: What is the second major purpose?
questions.answer: To let a person notice the many reflections of Allah’s sacred names in the world and believe through that awareness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes a person truly human?
questions.answer: Reaching these two purposes through gratitude, worship, recognition, and belief.

questions.question: What false view of success in life is criticized in this passage?
questions.answer: Thinking success means only living comfortably and pleasing the body.

questions.question: Why is that view presented as too low for a human being?
questions.answer: Because human beings were given special senses, feelings, and abilities for higher spiritual purposes.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the lower self’s desires?
questions.answer: They are base desires and should not be treated as the main goal of life.

questions.question: What is one purpose of the human faculties in relation to blessings?
questions.answer: They help a person notice the many gifts from Allah.

questions.question: After noticing those gifts, what should a person do?
questions.answer: Thank Allah and worship Him.

questions.question: What is another purpose of the faculties in relation to Allah’s names?
questions.answer: They help a person experience the different ways Allah’s names appear in the world.

questions.question: How should a person respond after recognizing those manifestations?
questions.answer: The person should come to faith.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying a person develops through these aims?
questions.answer: A person matures inwardly and becomes what a human being is meant to be.

questions.question: Why is ingratitude presented as a serious wrong?
questions.answer: Because blessings are meant to lead a person to thankfulness, not denial.

questions.question: What is the link between belief and the world around us in this passage?
questions.answer: The world contains signs that can lead a person to belief if they are noticed properly.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast sinners with the right use of life?
questions.answer: Sinners deny, insult, and misuse their gifts, while the right path is to recognize, thank, and believe.

questions.question: Write one sentence that gives the central lesson of the passage.
questions.answer: Human abilities should be used to know Allah through His blessings and signs, not wasted on temporary desires.

questions.question: What three wrong responses are mentioned about the sinful group at the start?
questions.answer: They responded with disbelief, ingratitude, and disrespect toward creation.

questions.question: What did they deny that made their crime especially serious?
questions.answer: They denied the manifestations of the divine names.

questions.question: What trust did they misuse?
questions.answer: They misused life itself and the abilities placed in human nature.

questions.question: What direct challenge is given to the reader’s inner self?
questions.answer: It asks whether the reader really thinks life is just for comfort and bodily pleasure.

questions.question: Which parts of the human being are named as having a higher purpose?
questions.answer: The senses, faculties, limbs, systems, feelings, and other inner abilities.

questions.question: What is the first of the two main aims of these God-given abilities?
questions.answer: To make Allah’s blessings known to a person so that the person gives thanks and worships.

questions.question: What does “the True Bestower” point to in simple words?
questions.answer: It points to Allah as the real Giver of blessings.

questions.question: What is the second of the two main aims?
questions.answer: To let a person know the signs of Allah’s names through experience and then believe.

questions.question: According to the passage, is belief meant to be blind and disconnected from experience? Explain.
questions.answer: No. The passage teaches that a person can experience the signs of Allah’s names and then recognize and believe in them.

questions.question: What kind of human being results from using these faculties correctly?
questions.answer: A mature and genuine human being.

questions.question: What warning does this passage give to a young reader?
questions.answer: Do not waste your life on low desires; use your gifts to know, thank, and worship Allah.

questions.question: When the passage speaks about entering the world at the age of discretion, what does that mean in simple terms?
questions.answer: It means reaching the stage when a person can understand choices and is responsible for them.

questions.question: How did the wicked group answer the signs pointing to tawhid?
questions.answer: They rejected them instead of accepting Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What was their response to the blessings they received?
questions.answer: They answered with ingratitude.

questions.question: How did their attitude toward creation show bad character?
questions.answer: They treated created things with contempt instead of seeing them as meaningful signs.

questions.question: What is the reason given for endless punishment?
questions.answer: They used the gifts of life and human ability to reject the One those gifts were meant to lead them to.

questions.question: What question does the passage ask about modern, comfortable living?
questions.answer: It asks whether a person thinks that kind of lifestyle is the whole duty of life.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention subtle senses and orderly body systems?
questions.answer: To show that human beings are carefully made for important purposes, not just appetite.

questions.question: What should recognizing different blessings lead to first?
questions.answer: It should lead to gratitude.

questions.question: What should gratitude then lead to?
questions.answer: It should lead to worship.

questions.question: What should recognizing the manifestations of Allah’s names lead to?
questions.answer: It should lead to faith.

questions.question: What two actions are expected from a person after learning these two aims?
questions.answer: To be aware of Allah’s gifts and to respond with thanks, worship, and belief.

questions.question: How would you summarize the difference between the sinners’ path and the right path?
questions.answer: The sinners misuse their gifts for denial and desire, while the right path uses those same gifts for gratitude and iman.

questions.question: What is the first big contrast in the passage between the sinful group and the proper use of life?
questions.answer: The sinful group uses life to deny and disrespect, while proper use of life leads to gratitude and belief.

questions.question: In the passage, what shows that creatures should not be treated as worthless?
questions.answer: They are connected to divine signs and blessings, so insulting them is a serious wrong.

questions.question: Why is denying the manifestations of the divine names such a heavy offense?
questions.answer: Because those manifestations are spread through life and the world, so denying them means rejecting many signs of Allah.

questions.question: What assumption about the body and its desires does the passage reject?
questions.answer: It rejects the idea that the body’s desires are the main reason humans were created.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the human being’s inner and outer abilities?
questions.answer: As fine, sensitive, ordered, and purposeful.

questions.question: What is one duty a person has after becoming aware of Allah’s blessings?
questions.answer: To thank Him.

questions.question: What is another duty after becoming aware of Allah’s blessings?
questions.answer: To worship Him.

questions.question: What role do human faculties play in recognizing Allah’s names?
questions.answer: They help a person notice and experience the ways His names appear in the world.

questions.question: After experiencing those manifestations, what should happen in the heart?
questions.answer: Faith should grow and become established.

questions.question: What does the passage say is the result of fulfilling the two main aims?
questions.answer: A person develops and reaches completion as a real human being.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect lesson is taught about human faculties?
questions.answer: If they are used rightly, they lead to gratitude and belief; if misused, they lead to serious wrongdoing.

questions.question: What advice from this passage would be most helpful for an eighth-grade Muslim student?
questions.answer: Do not live only for cravings and comfort; use your mind, senses, and heart to notice Allah’s gifts, thank Him, and strengthen your iman.
